MARKET.head: Moldova pitches indigenous grapes and 23 producers at ProWine Shanghai
MARKET.summ: With 23 wine and spirits producers heading to ProWine Shanghai, the export-driven country is putting indigenous grapes and competitive pricing at the center of its pitch
takeaways: Twenty-three Moldovan wine and spirits producers will seek Chinese importers and distributors at ProWine Shanghai, November 10 to 12.
Chinese customs data show Moldovan wine imports reached US$1.43 million in the first nine months of 2026.
About 85% of Moldova's production is exported, with the EU taking roughly 60% of wine exports.

MARKET.head: Australian wine's small formats gain ground as moderation and single-person households grow
MARKET.summ: Consumer demand for wine is changing globally, and while this has shown up in many mature markets as a decline in consumption, the shift in consumption habits has also uncovered an increasing consumer interest in smaller, more flexible packaging formats.
takeaways: Combined off-trade sales of 187mL wine packs rose 22 per cent to almost 1.9 million litres in 2025-26.
Export volumes of 187mL packs grew 39 per cent, from 450,000 litres in 2023-24 to 620,000 litres in 2025-26.
Single-person households make up 26 per cent of Australian households, up from 18 per cent in 1981, per Census data.

MARKET.head: EU greenwashing rules from September 27 restrict vague eco claims on wine labels and marketing
MARKET.summ: New restrictions on environmental marketing claims are putting terms like “natural” and “eco-friendly” under the microscope, prompting questions about what wineries can and can’t include on bottle labels
takeaways: EU Directive 2024/825, also called EmpCo, bans vague environmental claims on consumer products, with enforcement starting September 27.
Banned terms include generic words like eco-friendly and green, plus sustainability badges lacking independent third-party certification.
Enforcement is left to individual member states, with fines for widespread violations of up to four percent of annual turnover.

MARKET.head: Bordeaux takes 41% of fine wine trade value as Burgundy's share climbs
MARKET.summ: Bordeaux strengthened its lead of the market, claiming 41% of traded value. Burgundy’s share also rose compared to last week
takeaways: Bordeaux claimed 41% of the week's traded fine wine value, with 2019 and 2020 vintages top-traded by value.
Burgundy's share of traded value rose from 15.7% last week to 20.8%, with Domaine de la Romanée-Conti and Domaine Leflaive leading.
Champagne's share fell from 13.0% to 8.5%, while Tuscany claimed 11.6% of traded value, led by Soldera Case Basse and Sassicaia.

MARKET.head: India-EU trade deal cuts wine tariffs, but state rules still complicate entry
MARKET.summ: For years, India has occupied a peculiar position in the international wine industry: too large to ignore, too complicated to enter
takeaways: India's 150% tariff on EU wine will fall to 20% for premium and 30% for mid-range wines under the India-EU FTA.
Alcohol is regulated state by state in India, so exporters must plan market entry separately for each state.
India imported 5.4 million litres of wine worth US$28.8 million in 2025, up 13.7% in volume.

MARKET.head: California table grapes stay available through December for holiday promotions
MARKET.summ: Despite an early start to harvest, steady shipments and cold storage supplies are in position to keep California table grapes available for holiday promotions
takeaways: The California Table Grape Commission says grapes will stay in promotable volumes through December despite an early harvest.
Harvest is expected to end in mid-November, but significant volumes will keep shipping after picking concludes.
Commission research finds 72% of grape purchasers prefer U.S.-grown grapes, versus under 5% preferring imports.

CULTURE.head: Brendan Carter of Bottleshock named 2026 Wine Communicator of the Year
CULTURE.summ: Last night, Brendan Carter from Bottleshock was named the 2026 Wine Communicator of the Year by Wine Communicators of Australia (WCA). The announcement was the culmination of the celebrations at WCA’s sold out annual Awards Night in Sydney, with Brendan accepting his award from WCA National Chair, Lynda Schenk.
takeaways: Wine Communicators of Australia named Brendan Carter of Bottleshock its 2026 Wine Communicator of the Year at its Sydney Awards Night.
Judges reviewed entries from 33 industry professionals across 13 categories, with WCA National Chair Lynda Schenk presenting the award.
The award cited Carter's Bottleshock.TV and The Big Blind League wine tasting competition for engaging consumers in new ways.

CULTURE.head: Stanley Wine Bar wins three awards at 2026 Tasmanian wine list awards
CULTURE.summ: Stanley Wine Bar has emerged as the standout of the 2026 Tasmanian Wine List of the Year Awards, taking home three major accolades, including the coveted Overall Judges' Choice Best Tasmanian Wine List of the Year. The north-west coast gem also claimed Best Small Bar Wine List and, “proving the public agrees with the experts”,...
takeaways: Stanley Wine Bar on Tasmania's north-west coast took three honours at the 2026 Tasmanian Wine List of the Year Awards, presented by Wine Tasmania.
Its wins include Overall Judges' Choice Best Tasmanian Wine List of the Year, Best Small Bar Wine List and the People's Choice Award.
Judges were Curly Haslam-Coates of Vintage Tasmania, wine communicator Cassandra Camerer-Charlick, critic Nola James and Wine Tasmania.

CULTURE.head: Sixteen sommeliers name underrated Pinot Noir producers from Australia, Germany, Greece and beyond
CULTURE.summ: Though it has centuries of history in Burgundy, great quality Pinot Noir can now be found in every corner of the world, from the volcanic Otago peninsula in New Zealand to the high plateaus of Greece’s Amyndeon region. Across these different areas, Pinot Noir offers a wide variety of expressions, from dense, fruit-forward...
takeaways: Sixteen sommeliers were asked to name the most underrated Pinot Noir on the market right now.
Picks include Redbank from King Valley, Australia, and Wasenhaus and Enderle & Moll from Germany's Baden region.
Other picks range from Santa Cruz Mountains and San Luis Obispo Coast in California to Greece, Japan and Alto Adige.

CULTURE.head: Napa consultant launches one-day Thanksgiving wine Q&A staffed by industry experts
CULTURE.summ: A new project empowers curious holiday drinkers to ask real experts for their advice
takeaways: Evan Roscoe, a Napa social media consultant for wineries, launched Ask Wines, a 24-hour site running the day before Thanksgiving.
Visitors can ask human wine experts anything about buying, selecting, or pairing bottles for the holiday.
About 50 industry experts, including sommeliers, winemakers and buyers, volunteered within a day of his Instagram poll.

CULTURE.head: Alison Smith Story recounts her path into the wine business
CULTURE.summ: This episode of Wine 101 is brought to you by Wines of Alsace and Alsace Rocks. Tucked between the Vosges Mountains and the Rhine River in northeastern France, Alsace is one of the most distinctive wine regions on earth, and is home to centuries of family winemaking, some of France’s most certifiably organic vineyards, and a...
takeaways: Keith Beavers hosts this episode of VinePair's Wine 101 podcast, a casual conversation with Alison Smith Story of Smith Story Wine Cellars.
The episode covers how Smith Story came to work in the wine business rather than any market or production development.

CULTURE.head: Volcanic soils give wines a distinctive, tense character
CULTURE.summ:
Vines on volcanic soil are hard to grow and their grapes are hard-won, but it all combines to produce wines with a very particular sense of place

Good stories need jeopardy. Take The Princess Bride, one of my favourite films, which I recently introduced...
takeaways: Volcanic wine is a geological category, not a single style, covering soils such as ash, basalt, obsidian, pumice and tuff.
Importer Nic Rizzi of Modal Wines says volcanic wines carry an extra tension, which he attributes to hard farming conditions.
Victoria Torres Pecis makes wines on La Palma in the Canaries, where vines grow in black ash soils at 1,200m.

SCIENCE.head: Barossa workshop shows reworking old-vine Grenache takes patience, not haste
SCIENCE.summ: Last Thursday, a well-attended workshop discussing and demonstrating reworking old vine Grenache was held in the Barossa Valley. Hosted by The Barossa Viticulture Technical Group (BVTG) and led by technical viticulturist Tom Bartholomaeus as well as chief viticulturist Nigel Blieschke of Torbreck Vintners, the morning led...
takeaways: The Barossa Viticulture Technical Group ran a workshop led by Tom Bartholomaeus and Nigel Blieschke of Torbreck Vintners.
Block one, reworked in 2020, reached about 95% strike rate, while block two, reworked in 2022, managed only 75%.
Block two yielded roughly 1.3 tonnes per hectare less than block one, which the presenters blamed on rushing the process.

SCIENCE.head: Roller-crimped cover crops improve Mediterranean vine water status and mycorrhizal colonization
SCIENCE.summ: In a 2026 study published in Field Crops Research based on Mediterranean rainfed vineyards, the authors found that roller-crimping cover crops improved soil cover, vine water status, yield (in wetter conditions), and mycorrhizal colonization without affecting grape quality, while seasonal climate was the dominant driver of...
takeaways: A 2026 Field Crops Research study tested roller-crimped cover crops in rainfed Mediterranean vineyards.
Roller-crimping improved soil cover, vine water status and mycorrhizal colonization without affecting grape quality.
Yield rose only in wetter conditions, and seasonal climate was the main driver of fungal diversity.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Bordeaux 2024 vintage in bottle, assessing 100 of the top wines from this tricky vintage
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Once again, a chance to look through the latest Bordeaux vintage courtesy of the Union des Grands Crus at their
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jamie Goode
takeaways: The Union des Grands Crus London tasting presented the 2024 Bordeaux vintage, which the author calls difficult but with some fine wines.
Château de Fieuzal Pessac-Léognan Blanc 2024 scored 94/100, and Château Carbonnieux Pessac-Léognan Blanc 2024 scored 93/100.
The author judges the 2024 reds classically proportioned, perhaps lighter, and the whites really good, with the reds not expected to rise in price.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Catalonia’s Under(wine)world
NEWSLETTERS.summ: How a Champagne trip in the 1800s resulted in a new Spanish wine in a league of its own
NEWSLETTERS.author: Eveline Chartier
takeaways: Josep Raventós of Penedès produced Spain's first traditional method sparkling wine in 1872, using Spanish indigenous grapes rather than Champagne varieties.
Cava is produced mainly in Sant Sadurní d'Anoia, in Catalonia's Penedès region, where 95% of Cava comes from.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Roadshow Review: Spain Brings Value Wines to China
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Does any nation offer better wine value than Spain? This seems obvious to French bottlers, who import major amounts of Spanish wine each year. Per
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jim Boyce
takeaways: The Wines From Castilla, La Mancha Roadshow stopped in Beijing and was scheduled for Guangzhou on November 6.
Spain ranked fifth by volume in China last year, narrowly behind Italy, but only a quarter of leader Australia, per WBO stats.
Spain's value ranking in China fell to sixth, below New Zealand, with its per-liter value only above Chile among the top eight sources.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Why I Enjoy Wine Competition Judging
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Plus a guide to Le Puy wines - my notes from a recent vertical tasting
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: Columnist judged the Asia Wine Trophy in Daejeon, South Korea, on its dedicated orange and amber wine panel.
A Georgian Khikhvi amber was rated in the mid-90s by all six judges, earning grand gold without discussion.
Le Puy, a biodynamic right-bank Bordeaux estate, left the Francs Côtes de Bordeaux appellation in 2017 and now bottles as Vin de France.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Traditional labels? Suck My Duck
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Never say that wine labelling regulations are a subject devoid of humour. The Tribunal Correctionnel de Paris recently heard a case brought by anti-alcohol NGO Addictions France against Languedoc vigneron Nicolas Vellas over his provocative packaging. Vellas’s edgy cuvées have included “Little Fuck,” “Bad Angel” (its label...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: Paris court heard a case by anti-alcohol group Addictions France against Languedoc vigneron Nicolas Vellas over provocative labels like "Suck My Duck" and "Punish Me".
Bordeaux has lost a fifth of its vineyard area in four years, with about 30,000 ha to be uprooted by end of December, while its labels remain traditionally old-fashioned.
Author argues eye-catching labels from natural producers in less prestigious regions like the Loire, Beaujolais and Jura have attracted younger consumers.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Wine News: What I’m Reading the Week of 11/1/26
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Hello and welcome to my weekly roundup of the wine stories that I find of interest on the web. I
NEWSLETTERS.author: Alder Yarrow

NEWSLETTERS.head: The 2026 Harvest Is In , Here’s What It’s Already Telling Us About this Burgundy Wine Vintage
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Early harvest data from the 2026 Burgundy vintage reveals exciting insights into the region's grapes, offering a first look at vine yields and pricing
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jonathan Finch
takeaways: Burgundy's Côte d'Or picking finished between 10 and 12 September, after the region's earliest harvest ever recorded.
The Comité des Vins de Bourgogne estimates a crop drop of around 30 per cent against the five-year average; the official figure is due mid-November.
Growers report small, healthy berries with rich, balanced juice, while Agreste forecasts Pinot Noir losses in Burgundy of more than half.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Essential Kit for Kitchen Season
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Outfitting your kitchen with the season’s essential tools, plus this week’s favorite stories about food, wine, and culture
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Meg Maker says the clocks going back on Sunday marks the start of what she calls Kitchen Season.
During November and December, cooks feel a special itch to cook for others, per Meg Maker.
Meg Maker shares a list of kitchen tools she uses year-round that become more essential during festive cooking.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Tasting Diaries: October 2026
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Niagara’s Cabernet Franc harvest finally gets underway, plus the bottles that made my October memorable
NEWSLETTERS.author: Cab Franc Chronicles
takeaways: Niagara Peninsula Cabernet Franc is being harvested in October 2026, a little later than average, after one of the wettest summers on record.
Buttonwood Grove's 2025 Blanc de Franc from the Finger Lakes is praised as an off-dry white Cabernet Franc with about 10 g/L residual sugar.
Château de Fosse Sèche's 2018 Éolithe VDF from Saumur is described as fresh and elegant despite a warm vintage, with at least five years of life ahead.

NEWSLETTERS.head: A deeper look at underwater wine aging
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Is a wine from the depths ‘better’ or does it depend on the boat?
NEWSLETTERS.author: Miquel Hudin
takeaways: Attis, a winery owned by the Fariña family near Pontevedra, Galicia, ages magnums of its Albariño underwater in the O Grove estuary.
The underwater-aged bottling, Attis Albariño 'Mar', spends five months at 13-16C, versus the 'Standard' bottling of about 120,000 bottles annually.
The author's past tastings found underwater-aged wines tired and more advanced in age than landbound counterparts, which he judges a gimmick.
